The test image shows a sugarcane plant with severely bleached/whitened, dried-out leaves near the soil base. Key features:
- Complete leaf bleaching/scalding — straw/cream-white color throughout
- Leaves wilted and dried, with longitudinal pale streaks
- Browning at the stem base
- A round brownish object at ground level (possible rotting sett)
- Multiple tillers affected

Top candidates: **Leaf_Scald** (scalded/bleached leaves) or **Sett_Rot** (base rot killing tillers). I'll use my 1 reference view on Leaf_Scald.

The Leaf_Scald reference shows a classic white stripe/pencil-line pattern on a green leaf — that's NOT what I see in the test image.

The test image shows:
- **Complete bleaching/death** of all leaves (not a stripe pattern)
- A clearly visible **round brownish object at the base** — this looks like a rotting sett (seed piece)
- Stems browning and wilting near soil level
- Plant failing to establish — classic failure-to-emerge pattern

This matches **Sett_Rot**: the seed piece rots before the plant can establish, causing complete wilt and death of emerging shoots. The visible rotting sett at ground level is the key discriminating feature.
